meeting_header:
Date: 2028-01-22
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cole (Redwood SE), Ravi Kaur (Redwood CSM) -- Maya Chen (Orbitly Head of ML), Gustavo Ruiz (VP Eng), Lena Fischer (SRE), Tomoko Sato (Platform)
summary: Customer wants to extend current retainer (stretch capacity) + onboard Redwood nodes in EU (Ireland) and Japan (Tokyo). Discussed latency targets, burst pricing, fallback between hosted/dedicated, and data residency. Agreed next steps include updated quote, provisioning runbook, and technical kickoff in the week of Jan 30.
topics: Dedicated vs hosted for peak traffic
transcript:
[00:00] Samira (AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, uh quick agenda — pricing/term readout, node/region timing, then tech risks. we have about 45 minutes.
[00:15] Maya: thanks Samira, yep we just want to confirm numbers and make sure we don't break our latency SLOs for EU and JP.
[00:28] Ethan (SE): cool, quick framing — you've been on hosted today right? and you're looking to stretch the monthly retainer to cover predictable peak windows and add EU+JP nodes, correct?
[00:40] Gustavo: correct — hosted for prod now, we've had a couple of latency blips when traffic hits EU users and a big concern is Japan, we have localized customers there.
[00:52] Samira: great. so proposal we shared (pricing sheet link) shows two options — 1) small retainer stretch + on-demand burst; 2) dedicated pool in EU + shared hosted in JP as a stopgap. both include standard SLA uplift for the dedicated option.
[01:10] Lena: can you clarify the SLA uplift — is that latency p95 or p99? our SRE wants p95 under 300ms for EU region for our low-latency flows.
[01:25] Ethan: yes for dedicated we guarantee p95 target in our SLO docs, usually the commit is for p95 token latency under the configured seq length distribution — but small caveat is tail behavior with very large system prompts. we'll show some RW bench numbers.
[01:42] Maya: when you say bench numbers, is that internal benchmarking or something we can run? we want us to run a smoke bench with our prompt set.
[01:50] Ethan: absolutely — we can run a customer-facing bench. we'll need a small corpus and your typical seq lens. we'll run on both quantized variants and a full fp16 path to compare latency/cost.
[02:04] Gustavo: okay, and about data — we need audit logs exported to our SIEM and KMS integration. is that part of the private offering?
[02:14] Ravi (CSM): yes we have KMS integrations (customer-managed keys) for Private, for Hosted we support envelope encryption but audit log forwarding is an add-on, we can include a sample syslog S3 flow.
[02:28] Tomoko: we have strict egress through corporate proxy; can Redwood agents originate from within our VPC or do we have to do NAT rules?
[02:36] Ethan: for Private/VPC we install a customer-side control plane and your nodes sit in your VPC — so traffic egress is under your control. for Hosted we'd need firewall rules to allow outbound to Redwood endpoints. we'll share a firewall checklist.
[02:52] Maya: about timing — ideally EU live by mid-February and JP pilot by end of March. are those realistic?
[03:00] Samira: EU mid-February is tight but doable if PO lands this week; JP by end of March is achievable but depends on capacity reservations in the APAC pool — we'll need to confirm the GPU availability.
[03:15] Gustavo: what's the procurement path? are we doing a one-off amendment to extend term or new PO?
[03:21] Samira: we can do an amendment to existing Master Services Agreement for a retainer stretch; I'll send the PO template so your procurement can review.
[03:32] Lena: price delta on dedicated vs hosted — roughly how much more?
[03:36] Ethan: ballpark: dedicated is often 1.6x-2x per-token cost at low utilization but gives you predictable latency and reserved throughput; with bin packing and batching optimizations Redwood Optimize suggests quantization that can cut that gap. also autoscaling burst credits reduce effective price for spiky workloads.
[03:56] Maya: are there fallback policies if a dedicated pool goes down? we'd like automatic fallback to a compatible hosted variant.
[04:03] Ethan: yes we have smart routing and automatic fallback — we can set policy to failover to a lighter quantized hosted model in same region or to nearest region; we'll include suggested policy in the runbook.
[04:18] Gustavo: any competitor issues — we evaluated Anthropic but they didn't have our desired EU footprint; VectorServe promised on-prem but not at scale.
[04:30] Samira: noted. Redwood's differentiator here is the unified tooling — same api surface for hosted/dedicated/private and first-class rollouts.
[04:41] Maya: on compliance — SOC two, and we need 1-year audit-able logs. does Redwood retain full transcription or just metadata?
[04:52] Ravi: we retain request/response metadata and full logs are available via enterprise retention add-on — searchable by token window for evals. we can map retention to your policy.
[05:05] Tomoko: tech question — will the KV cache persist across warm restarts in dedicated? we've seen cold start penalties in other setups.
[05:14] Ethan: KV cache is preserved within a serving shard; we do warm handoffs and pre-warming for scheduled scale-ups. cold restarts can be mitigated by prefix caching and predictive warmers, we'll outline the knobs.
[05:30] Lena: about monitoring — can we get token-level cost by route?
[05:36] Ravi: yes console has token-level breakdown, per-route dashboards, you can export to Datadog or BigQuery.
[05:45] Maya: next steps quick recap?
[05:48] Samira: sure. we'll a) send updated quote with the two options and the amendment language, b) SE to run bench with Orbitly prompts for EU and JP, c) customer to confirm traffic split and proc timeline.
[06:05] Gustavo: ok. one ask — can you include a brief cost sensitivity table (latency vs price) that we can present to execs?
[06:12] Samira: yes we'll include a simple sensitivity table in the quote.
[06:20] Ethan: one more technical note — for JP we may recommend starting with hosted tier for initial pilot to avoid long lead times on dedicated GPU procurement, then convert to dedicated after pilot. that balances speed vs price.
[06:35] Tomoko: fine with that approach.
[06:38] Maya: thanks everyone, we appreciate the flexibility. we'll aim to get the PO to you by Thursday.
[06:44] Samira: great — we'll follow up with the artifacts: updated quote (link), provisioning runbook (link), bench instructions (link). thanks all.
[06:52] [END]
